info.title: Singa Merchant API
info.description: OpenAPI specification for the merchant/partner HTTP API. All routes below are additionally protected by `ip.whitelisted.merchant` — the caller IP must be registered for the credential or merchant. Obtain a JWT using `POST /api/v1.0/access-token/b2b` (Basic auth) or `POST /api/v1.1/access-token/b2b` (X-Signature) before calling secured endpoints.

post.description:
Transfers funds from the given PG account (remitter) to a beneficiary under the same merchant. Compatible-extend contract: omit `beneficiary_channel` (or set `PG`) and pass `beneficiary_account_number` for intra-PG movement; set `beneficiary_channel=KYC` to credit the merchant KYC credit-pool. `BILLER` is reserved. Requires request signature headers (`verify.signature-internal`).

Idempotency: send an optional `merchant_ref_no` unique per merchant. If a value already used by the same merchant is submitted again, the original transfer is returned (HTTP 200) and no new movement is created — regardless of which of the merchant's accounts is the remitter. If `merchant_ref_no` is omitted or empty, the platform auto-generates a unique reference (format `AM-<timestamp>-<random>`) and returns it in the response.

get.description: This feature is designed to provide detailed information regarding the list of virtual accounts. It allows users to retrieve and view comprehensive data on all virtual accounts associated with their main account. Each managed sub account row carries its own `kyb_onboarding_url` so its current active KYB self-onboarding link can be read directly from the list without a separate call per account.

post.description: Create a new sub account under the calling merchant. `account_type` is required — choose between an `owned`/`personal_managed` sub account (created active, no KYB — `personal_managed` behaves the same as `owned`) and a `business_managed` sub account (created inactive and requiring BOSS KYB approval before it can transact). The calling merchant's own primary dashboard login is always granted access to the new account automatically. `invite_members` is optional — pass additional member emails to grant them access too; if omitted, only the primary merchant has access. For a `business_managed` sub account, `data.kyb_onboarding_url` carries a link to forward to the sub-merchant so they can self-submit their KYB data (individual/company is chosen on that onboarding page itself). Save this URL, as it becomes `null` once KYB is verified; it can also be re-fetched anytime via `GET /accounts/{id}` or `GET /accounts` while KYB is still pending.

get.description: This feature is designed to provide detailed information regarding the details of a virtual account. Note: a `managed` sub account cannot be set to `active` until its BOSS KYB verification is approved — attempting to do so returns 403.

post.description: Initiates a cardless withdrawal, debits the account, and returns an OTP for ATM cash collection. Only fixed denominations (multiples of 50,000) are accepted. The target account is specified in the request body (`account_id`), not in the URL path. This endpoint is rate-limited. See `Response Code` for SP000–SP020 definitions and merchant actions. **CRITICAL:** This is a money-out operation requiring **X-Signature** and **X-Timestamp** authentication.

parameters.name: X-Signature
parameters.description: HMAC-SHA512 hex signature, computed as `HMAC_SHA512(clientSecret, "{HTTP_METHOD}:{REQUEST_URI}:{ACCESS_TOKEN}:{SHA256_HEX(MINIFIED_BODY)}:{X_TIMESTAMP}")`. `MINIFIED_BODY` is the request body with object keys recursively sorted alphabetically and re-serialised with no whitespace. `ACCESS_TOKEN` is the bearer token without the `Bearer ` prefix. Missing header returns **422** (`response_code=SP018`); signature mismatch returns **401** (`response_code=SP016`).

parameters.name: X-Timestamp
parameters.description: Timestamp of the request; used as part of the signed string. Missing header returns **422** (`response_code=SP018`).

requestBody.description: Target account, reference number, customer details, withdrawal amount, and payment channel selection.

200.description: **SP000** Successfully — withdrawal initiated (`data.transaction_status.code` is `01`). The `data.otp_number` holds the OTP for ATM redemption. Note: `data.balance_after` is always `"0"` on this response — it is not the actual post-debit balance; use the show or list endpoint to read the real account balance.

400.description: **SP004** Duplicate Reference Number, or **SP011** Beneficiary Vendor Not Active (no active cardless withdrawal vendor), or **SP003** Insufficient Balance. Merchant action: use a new `reference_number` for SP004; check balance for SP003.

data.message: Transaction with this reference number already exists

403.description: **SP003** Insufficient Balance, detected on a re-check performed while the account is locked. Only reachable under concurrent requests against the same account; the initial balance check (before locking) returns **400** instead. `data` reflects a `failed` transaction (`transaction_status.code` `06`).

post.description: Initiates a Direct Debit binding flow. The merchant must redirect the customer to `data.redirect_url` to complete bank authentication; the link is single-use and expires at `data.expires_at` (typically ~15 minutes). Final binding outcome is delivered via the configured `direct_debit_notif_url` callback.

200.description: **SP000** Successfully — `data` matches `DirectDebitBindingInitiationData`. The customer must open `redirect_url` to authenticate.

403.description: IP not on the merchant allowlist (`ip.whitelisted.merchant`).

422.description: **SP018** Validation error — missing/invalid field in the request body. Field details are in `data.errors`.

500.description: **SP002** General Failure — upstream gateway call could not be completed. Retry with the same payload (idempotent on `customer_ref` while the previous binding is still `PENDING_AUTH`).

get.description: Returns the current state of a binding. Use this endpoint to poll for `PENDING_AUTH → ACTIVE` transitions when webhook delivery is unavailable; otherwise prefer the `direct-debit.binding.succeeded` callback. `{binding_id}` is constrained to UUID at the route layer, so malformed values return **404** before controller execution.

parameters.name: binding_id
parameters.description: UUID of a `DirectDebitBinding` owned by the authenticated merchant.

404.description: **SP014** Not Found — binding does not exist or belongs to another merchant.

post.description: Revokes an active binding. After this completes the binding can no longer be charged. Some banks require OTP; in that case the response is **HTTP 202** with `data.otp_required=true` and an `otp_handoff` block, and the merchant must follow up with `POST /verify-otp`. Other banks use a fire-and-forget flow; the binding remains in its current `status` until the `direct-debit.unbinding.succeeded` webhook confirms the final state. No request body is required.

parameters.name: binding_id
parameters.description: UUID of a `DirectDebitBinding` owned by the authenticated merchant.

200.description: **SP000** Successfully — unbinding initiated (fire-and-forget). `data` matches `DirectDebitBindingData`; `status` flips to `UNBOUND` only after the `direct-debit.unbinding.succeeded` callback lands.

202.description: **SP000** Successfully — OTP required. `data` matches `DirectDebitUnbindOtpRequiredData`. Persist `otp_handoff` and submit it back through `POST /verify-otp` along with the OTP the customer received.

404.description: **SP014** Not Found — binding not found for this merchant.

500.description: **SP002** General Failure — the gateway rejected the unbind request before we could persist a state.

get.description: Returns the latest known state of a Direct Debit charge. If the row remains non-terminal beyond the configurable reconciliation window, this endpoint attempts an upstream reconcile before responding so the result is as fresh as possible. Reconcile failures are logged and the existing record is still returned. `{transaction_id}` is constrained to UUID at the route layer.

parameters.name: transaction_id
parameters.description: UUID of a `DirectDebitTransaction` owned by the authenticated merchant.

200.description: **SP000** Successfully — `data` matches `DirectDebitTransactionData`. `fees` is populated **only** when `status=SUCCESS`; absent (not zero) on `PENDING`, `PENDING_OTP`, `FAILED`, and `EXPIRED`.

data.description: Subscription June 2026

post.description: Completes OTP verification for either payment or unbinding flows. Use `transaction_id` for payment OTP (after `POST /charge` returns `requires_otp=true`), or `binding_id` + `unbind_context` for unbind OTP (after `POST /binding/{id}/unbind` returns `otp_handoff`). Submitting both or neither returns **422 SP018**.

200.description: **SP000** Successfully. For the **payment** flow, `data` matches `DirectDebitTransactionData` and `status` moves `PENDING_OTP → PENDING` (final `SUCCESS` arrives via webhook). For the **unbinding** flow, `data` matches `DirectDebitBindingData`; the binding stays `ACTIVE` until the `direct-debit.unbinding.succeeded` callback flips it to `UNBOUND`.

400.description: **SP001** Transaction Failure — wrong OTP, expired OTP (~3 min TTL), or upstream rejected verification.

404.description: **SP009** Transaction Not Found (payment OTP) or **SP014** Not Found (binding / unbind OTP).

post.description: Validates a beneficiary's e-wallet account details and retrieves applicable transfer limits and fee information. This endpoint queries the e-wallet provider gateway to verify account validity and calculate transaction fees. Use this endpoint before initiating an actual transfer to ensure the account exists and meets your requirements. Optional **X-Signature** and **X-Timestamp** headers are required when your integration uses internal request signing.

Retrieves the current status of a previously initiated e-wallet transfer. This endpoint looks up the transaction by reference number and returns detailed status information. For transactions still in Pending status, the endpoint may query the e-wallet provider for updated status information. Status codes include 00 (Success), 03 (Pending), and 06 (Failed). Network timeouts during provider status checks will result in error code SP005.

Initiates an e-wallet fund transfer to a beneficiary. This endpoint performs comprehensive validation, deducts funds from merchant balance atomically, creates a transaction record, and queues processing through the job system. The response indicates transaction has been queued with status typically Pending until background processing completes. **CRITICAL:** This is a money-out operation requiring **X-Signature** and **X-Timestamp** authentication per internal signing protocol. Middleware validation includes kill-switch check, request signature verification, rate limiting, and anomaly detection. Duplicate reference numbers within 24 hours are rejected with error code SP004.

AccountTransferRequestBody.description: Compatible-extend contract: PG→PG still uses `beneficiary_account_number`. Cross-channel (KYC / future BILLER) sets `beneficiary_channel` and omits the PG account number. Optional `beneficiary_account_id` is reserved for multi-pool peer products.

amount.description: Transfer amount in IDR. Must be at least 1 and not exceed the remitter account available balance.

beneficiary_channel.description: Destination product channel. Omit or `PG` for intra-PG movement. `KYC` credits the merchant KYC credit-pool. `BILLER` is not enabled yet.

beneficiary_account_number.description: Required when beneficiary_channel is PG (or omitted). 12-digit PG account number of the destination account; must belong to the same merchant and be active.

beneficiary_account_id.description: Optional peer-product account selector. Unused for KYC today (one pool per merchant). Reserved for future multi-pool / BILLER.

merchant_ref_no.description: Optional merchant-supplied idempotency reference. Unique per merchant across all account movements: reusing a value already used by the same merchant returns the original transfer (HTTP 200) without creating a duplicate. If omitted or empty, the platform auto-generates a unique reference (format `AM-<timestamp>-<random>`) and returns it in the response — a generated reference is unique per request and therefore provides no replay protection. A different merchant may reuse the same value.

transaction_id.description: Unique transaction identifier generated by the platform.

merchant_ref_no.description: Merchant-supplied idempotency reference echoed back, or null if none was provided.

status.description: Transaction status. Always `success` for completed transfers.

amount.description: Transfer amount.

value.description: Amount as string to preserve decimal precision.

beneficiary.description: Destination account details. For KYC/BILLER, account_id/account_number identify the peer credit-pool.

account_id.description: Beneficiary PG ULID, or peer credit-pool account id.

account_name.description: Beneficiary account name, or peer pool label.

account_number.description: Beneficiary PG account number, or peer credit-pool account number.

processed_timestamp.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when the transfer was processed.

created_at.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when the record was created.

AccountTransferSuccessEnvelope.description: Standard success response envelope for account transfer endpoints.

pagination.description: Pagination metadata for list endpoints; omitted for single-object responses.

status.description: Account status. `active` accounts can transact. `owned`/`personal_managed` accounts are created `active`; `business_managed` accounts are created `inactive` and only become `active` after BOSS KYB approval.

account_type.description: Sub account type. `owned` = fully owned by the parent merchant (no KYB, active immediately). `personal_managed` behaves the same as `owned` (no KYB, active immediately). `business_managed` = third-party business managed by the parent merchant (requires BOSS KYB approval before it can transact). `null` for legacy accounts created before this field existed.

kyb_status.description: KYB status for managed sub accounts only. `kyb_waiting_document` = nothing submitted yet, waiting for the sub-merchant to fill the KYB form via `kyb_onboarding_url`. `kyb_in_review` = data submitted, under review (document/DTTOT/blacklist stage). `kyb_rejected` = a review stage rejected it; see `kyb_rejection_reason`, resubmit to go back to `kyb_in_review`. `kyb_verified` = approved, account can transact. `null` for owned/legacy accounts. `kyb_rejected` is also delivered in real time via the `kyb.rejected` webhook event — this field lets a merchant get the same information by polling instead.

kyb_rejection_reason.description: Reason text for the rejection when `kyb_status` is `kyb_rejected`. `null` otherwise.

legal_name.description: Legal name for a `business_managed` sub account, populated only once its KYB is `kyb_verified`. For `business_type` `company`, this is the legal company name. For `business_type` `individual`, this is the primary owner's full name. `null` for `owned`/`personal_managed` accounts (none of which require KYB), or a `business_managed` account not yet verified.

business_type.description: For `business_managed` accounts only: whether the sub-merchant self-onboarded as an individual/sole proprietorship or a registered company — chosen during KYB self-onboarding. `null` until the sub-merchant makes this choice, and always `null` for `owned`/`personal_managed` accounts.

brand_name.description: Brand name for a managed sub account, populated only once its KYB is `kyb_verified`. `null` for owned accounts, managed accounts not yet verified, or when no brand name was provided during KYB.

kyb_onboarding_url.description: KYB self-onboarding link for a `business_managed` sub account — a public, token-gated, single active link per account. The same URL stays valid across submit/reject/resubmit cycles until KYB is fully verified. On create, this is a freshly generated link; on `GET /accounts/{id}` and `GET /accounts`, it re-surfaces the account's current active link. `null` for `owned`/`personal_managed` accounts (none of which require KYB), or once KYB is fully verified (the link is revoked at that point).

invite_members.description: List of email addresses of dashboard members who have access to this account.

account_type.description: Required. Sub account type. `owned`/`personal_managed` create the account `active` immediately (no KYB). `business_managed` creates the account `inactive` and requires BOSS KYB approval before the account can transact.

invite_members.description: Optional. Array of additional merchant member email addresses to grant access to this account, on top of the calling merchant's own primary dashboard login (always granted access automatically, whether or not this field is provided). All emails must belong to registered members of the merchant. If omitted, only the primary merchant has access.

name.description: Optional. New account name. Omit to leave the current name unchanged.

status.description: Optional. Target account status. Omit to leave the current status unchanged.

invite_members.description: Optional. Array of team member email addresses to grant access to this account. This replaces the entire member list — any existing members not included will lose access. Omit the field to leave current members unchanged. All emails must belong to registered members of the merchant.

held_balance.description: Funds held on this account and not available for withdrawal.

available_balance.description: Funds available on this account for immediate use.

pending_balance.description: Amounts pending settlement for this account.

balance.description: Total ledger balance for this account.

account_id.description: ULID (Universally Unique Lexicographically Sortable Identifier) of the account this balance belongs to.

CreateCardOneTimePaymentRequest.description: Request payload for a one-time card payment (full or installment). Customer billing details and card credentials are mandatory; installment fields are optional.

amount.description: Charge amount in IDR (whole number). Must be within the limits defined by `config(default_money_in_out.min_card_amount|max_card_amount)`.

reference_no.description: Merchant reference for the transaction. Auto-generated when omitted.

goods_name.description: Name or description of the goods/service being purchased.

customer_name.description: Full name of the paying customer.

customer_country.description: Customer country as a 2-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.

description.description: Optional free-text note for the transaction.

card_number.description: Card primary account number (PAN). Spaces are stripped before processing.

card_cvv.description: Card verification value (CVV/CVC) printed on the card.

card_holder_name.description: Cardholder name as printed on the card.

installment.description: Set to `true` to pay by installment. Defaults to `false` (full payment).

installment_month.description: Installment tenor in months. Required only when `installment` is `true`.

CardPaymentData.description: Payload returned on a one-time payment request (`CardPaymentMerchantApiService::mapPaymentResponseToV2`). When the card requires 3-D Secure, `action` is `redirect` and the merchant must forward the customer to `payment_url`; otherwise `action` is `complete`.

provider_auth_no.description: Authorization number returned by the issuer.

result_code.description: Raw provider result code (`0000` indicates success).

action.description: Next step for the merchant: `redirect` (3-D Secure required) or `complete`.

requires_3ds.description: Present and `true` when 3-D Secure authentication is required.

payment_url.description: 3-D Secure redirect URL / HTML form. Present only when `action` is `redirect`.

html_form.description: Raw 3-D Secure HTML form. Present only when `action` is `redirect`.

immediate_success.description: Present when `action` is `complete`; `true` when the payment was authorized without 3-D Secure.

CardCancelData.description: Payload returned on a successful cancel. `cancel_type` is `void` for a not-yet-settled transaction or `refund` for a settled one.

cancel_type.description: Cancellation type applied by the provider.

CardInquiryStatusData.description: Payload returned on a status inquiry. Provider fields are populated once the transaction has reached the provider.

amount.description: Transaction amount in IDR.

provider_auth_no.description: Authorization number returned by the issuer.

provider_result_code.description: Raw provider result code (`0000` indicates success).

completed_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the transaction succeeded.

failed_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the transaction failed.

CardPaymentSuccessResponse.description: Merchant v2 envelope returned on a successful one-time payment request (`SP000`, HTTP 200).

CardCancelSuccessResponse.description: Merchant v2 envelope returned on a successful cancel (`SP000`, HTTP 200).

CardInquiryStatusSuccessResponse.description: Merchant v2 envelope returned on a successful status inquiry (`SP000`, HTTP 200).

CardErrorBadRequestResponse.description: Merchant v2 envelope for validation or bad-request failures (`SP012`, HTTP 400). Validation failures include `data.errors` keyed by field name.

data.description: Validation context. Present on input validation failures.

amount: The amount must be at least 10000.

CardErrorTransactionFailureResponse.description: Merchant v2 envelope when the provider declines or the transaction cannot be processed (`SP001`, HTTP 400). `data.status` reflects the resulting transaction state.

CardErrorTransactionNotFoundResponse.description: Merchant v2 envelope when the referenced transaction does not exist for this account (`SP009`, HTTP 404).

CardErrorAccountNotFoundResponse.description: Merchant v2 envelope when the `{account_id}` does not belong to the authenticated merchant (`SP020`, HTTP 404).

CardErrorAccessDeniedResponse.description: Merchant v2 envelope when the authenticated merchant is not allowed to access this account (HTTP 403). Returned by the controller with a numeric `403` response code.

CardErrorGeneralFailureResponse.description: Merchant v2 envelope for unexpected server-side failures (`SP002`, HTTP 500).

CreateCardlessWithdrawalRequest.description: Request body for initiating a new cardless withdrawal transaction. The target account is specified in the body (`account_id`), not in the URL path.

account_id.description: Unique identifier (ULID) of the merchant account to debit. The account must be active and belong to the authenticated merchant.

reference_number.description: Unique merchant reference for this withdrawal within the account. Used for idempotency; a duplicate reference returns HTTP 400 with response code SP004.

customer_name.description: Name of the end customer performing the ATM withdrawal.

customer_id.description: Merchant-side identifier of the end customer.

amount.description: Net withdrawal amount in IDR. Must be a multiple of 50,000, between 50,000 and 1,000,000 inclusive. Values that are not a multiple of 50,000 return HTTP 422 with response code SP018.

vendor_code.description: Code identifying the cardless withdrawal payment channel. Contact support for the list of available vendor codes.

CancelCardlessWithdrawalRequest.description: Request body for canceling an open cardless withdrawal transaction.

account_id.description: Unique identifier (ULID) of the merchant account. Must be active and belong to the authenticated merchant.

reference_number.description: Merchant reference of the withdrawal to cancel. Lookup is scoped to the account and only matches a transaction currently in `open` status.

CardlessWithdrawalTransactionStatus.description: Mapped withdrawal status returned in create and cancel responses.

code.description: Two-digit status code: `00` Success, `01` Initiated, `03` Pending, `04` Refunded, `05` Canceled, `06` Failed, `07` Not Found.

CardlessWithdrawalCustomer.description: End-customer information echoed in create and cancel responses.

CardlessWithdrawalMoneyAmount.description: Monetary amount in cardless withdrawal create and cancel responses.

value.description: Amount as a decimal string in IDR.

CardlessWithdrawalTransactionData.description: `data` on successful create or cancel (HTTP 200, `response_code` SP000).

reference_number.description: Merchant reference supplied in the request.

post_timestamp.description: Transaction creation time as a 13-digit Unix timestamp in milliseconds (string).

processed_timestamp.description: Processing time as a 13-digit Unix timestamp in milliseconds (string). Empty on create; the cancellation time on cancel.

expired_at.description: On create, the OTP expiry time as a 13-digit Unix timestamp in milliseconds (string). On cancel, this field is reused to carry the cancellation timestamp instead — it is not an expiry.

otp_number.description: One-time password the customer enters at the ATM. Present only in the create response; always empty on cancel.

vendor_code.description: Payment channel code from the request.

gross_amount.description: Total debited from the merchant account (net amount plus fee).

fee.description: Combined vendor and platform fee for the withdrawal.

net_amount.description: Net withdrawal amount requested by the merchant.

balance_after.description: On a successful create, this is always hardcoded to `"0"` by the controller — it does not reflect the actual post-debit balance. On cancel, it reflects the real merchant account balance after the debited amount is restored. On the insufficient-balance race-condition response (HTTP 403), the value is an empty string.

MerchantV2ApiEnvelopeCardlessWithdrawal.description: Custom v2 envelope for cardless withdrawal create and cancel. Success uses `SP000` (HTTP 200).

CardlessWithdrawalResource.description: Cardless withdrawal transaction record returned by the list and show endpoints (`CardlessWithdrawalTransformer`). Field set and names differ from the create/cancel `data` shape (`CardlessWithdrawalTransactionData`) — these are two distinct response contracts for the same underlying transaction.

transaction_id.description: Unique transaction identifier assigned by the platform.

reference_number.description: Merchant-supplied reference number provided when the withdrawal was created. Use this value (not `transaction_id`) as the `{reference_number}` path parameter on the show endpoint.

status.description: Raw transaction lifecycle status column. Values seen in practice: `open` — awaiting OTP redemption at ATM (the initial status on create, despite `CardlessWithdrawalStatus::PENDING` enum value being `pending`); `success` — funds withdrawn; `expired` — OTP expired before redemption; `failed` — withdrawal failed; `refunded` — funds returned to merchant; `canceled` — merchant canceled the withdrawal.

amount.description: Net withdrawal amount in IDR (the denomination selected by the merchant, excluding fees).

fee.description: Platform service fee (`our_margin` column) applied to the transaction, in IDR. Does not include the separate vendor/bank fee.

total_paid.description: Total amount debited from the merchant account in IDR (net amount plus fees).

balance_after.description: Merchant account balance (in IDR) immediately after this withdrawal was processed or, once canceled, after the debited amount was restored.

otp_expired_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp indicating when the OTP expires. The customer must complete the ATM withdrawal before this time.

customer_id.description: Merchant-side identifier of the end customer, as supplied on create.

customer_name.description: End customer name, as supplied on create.

location.description: ATM/CRM terminal name and location (`terminal_name_location` column). Populated by the vendor webhook once the withdrawal is redeemed; `null` while still `open`.

processed_at.description: Timestamp when the transaction reached a final state (success/failed/canceled). `null` while still `open`.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the withdrawal was created.

oneOf.description: Related account resource. Only present on the show endpoint response (list does not include it).

account.description: Related account resource. Only present on the show endpoint response (list does not include it).

ResponderSuccessCardlessWithdrawal.description: Success response envelope for cardless withdrawal endpoints returning a single transaction record.

status.description: HTTP status code echoed in the response body.

success.description: Indicates whether the request completed successfully.

data.description: The cardless withdrawal transaction record.

ResponderSuccessCardlessWithdrawalList.description: Success response envelope for the cardless withdrawal list endpoint. Contains a paginated collection of withdrawal records.

status.description: HTTP status code echoed in the response body.

success.description: Indicates whether the request completed successfully.

data.description: Array of cardless withdrawal transaction records.

pagination.description: Pagination metadata including current page, per page count, and total records.

count.description: Number of records returned in this page.

total.description: Total number of records matching the query.

perPage.description: Maximum number of records per page.

CreateDirectDebitBindingRequest.description: Initiates a Direct Debit binding flow. The merchant must redirect the customer to the returned `redirect_url` to complete bank authentication. `bank_code` is optional; when omitted the hosted webview renders a bank picker. `payment_otp_mode` is a preferred charge-time mode and the bank may still enforce its own OTP rules.

customer_ref.description: Merchant-side stable id for the customer (NOT the bank account number). Used to scope future bindings of the same customer.

phone_no.description: Customer mobile phone in E.164-ish form (e.g. `+6281234567890`). The bank may use this to deliver OTP.

bank_code.description: 3-digit BI/SNAP code of the target bank. Common values: `002` BRI, `008` Mandiri, `009` BNI, `011` Danamon, `014` BCA, `022` CIMB, `490` BNC.

payment_otp_mode.description: Preferred OTP behavior for later charge requests. The actual bank flow may still require OTP regardless of this hint.

success_redirect_url.description: Where the hosted webview redirects after a successful authorization.

failure_redirect_url.description: Where the hosted webview redirects after a failed/cancelled authorization.

DirectDebitChargeRequest.description: Pulls funds from an active binding into the merchant settlement account identified by `account_id`. The binding must be `ACTIVE`. `merchant_reference` is an idempotency key; replaying the same value returns **409 SP004** with the original `transaction_id` in `data`.

account_id.description: ULID of the merchant settlement account that should receive the funds. Must be owned by the authenticated merchant; access policy on the account is also enforced.

binding_id.description: UUID of an `ACTIVE` `DirectDebitBinding` owned by the merchant.

merchant_reference.description: Merchant-side unique idempotency key for this charge.

amount.description: Amount to debit, in the unit of `currency`. Minimum **10,000 IDR** (Ayoconnect Direct Debit floor).

currency.description: ISO-4217. Defaults to `IDR` (the only value supported by Direct Debit).

description.description: Customer-facing description for this charge. This value is stored with the transaction and may appear in reports.

DirectDebitVerifyOtpRequest.description: Submits an OTP to complete either a payment authorization or an unbind operation. Use `transaction_id` for payment-OTP flows, or `binding_id` + `unbind_context` for unbind-OTP flows. Exactly one of these flow definitions must be present.

transaction_id.description: Required for the payment-OTP flow; the id returned by `POST /charge` when `requires_otp=true`.

binding_id.description: Required for the unbinding-OTP flow; together with `unbind_context` from the original `/unbind` response.

otp.description: OTP value the customer received from their bank.

oneOf.description: Verbatim `otp_handoff` block returned by `POST /binding/{binding_id}/unbind` (when `otp_required=true`). Required for the unbinding-OTP flow.

unbind_context.description: Verbatim `otp_handoff` block returned by `POST /binding/{binding_id}/unbind` (when `otp_required=true`). Required for the unbinding-OTP flow.

DirectDebitUnbindOtpHandoff.description: Context required to complete an OTP-gated unbinding. Returned by `/binding/{binding_id}/unbind` (HTTP 202) and submitted back through `/verify-otp`. Singapay mints a fresh vendor `X-EXTERNAL-ID` on verify — merchants do not supply one.

flow.description: Flow type, always `UNBINDING` for this response.

partner_reference_no.description: Partner reference number returned by the downstream gateway for the unbind session.

reference_no.description: Gateway reference number for the unbind attempt, when available.

otp_token.description: OTP session token tied to this unbind attempt; typically valid for ~3 minutes.

DirectDebitBindingStatus.description: Lifecycle of a `DirectDebitBinding`. `PENDING_AUTH` → `ACTIVE` (customer authorised at bank) → `UNBOUND` (revoked). Terminal failure paths: `FAILED` (cancel/reject during auth) and `EXPIRED` (`redirect_url` not used in time).

DirectDebitTransactionStatus.description: Lifecycle of a `DirectDebitTransaction`. `PENDING` (charge accepted, awaiting settlement callback), `PENDING_OTP` (waiting for `/verify-otp`), `SUCCESS` (funds credited; `fees` populated), `FAILED` (final rejection), `EXPIRED` (OTP not submitted in time or upstream timeout).

DirectDebitBindingInitiationData.description: `data` payload returned by `POST /binding`. The merchant frontend must redirect the customer to `redirect_url` immediately; the link is single-use and expires at `expires_at` (typically ~15 minutes).

binding_id.description: ID of the binding being created; used for subsequent polling or OTP verification.

customer_ref.description: Merchant-side stable id for the customer (NOT the bank account number). Used to scope future bindings of the same customer.

bank_code.description: 3-digit BI/SNAP code of the target bank. Common values: `002` BRI, `008` Mandiri, `009` BNI, `011` Danamon, `014` BCA, `022` CIMB, `490` BNC.

redirect_url.description: Hosted webview URL the customer must open to authenticate with their bank. **Treat this URL as opaque** — do not parse, hardcode, or pattern-match on its host or path; both can change without notice. Open it in a webview/browser as-is and rely on the binding webhook (or polling `GET /binding/{binding_id}`) for the final outcome.

expires_at.description: Expiration time of the `redirect_url`. The customer must complete authentication before this time; otherwise the URL becomes invalid and the binding attempt is cancelled.

payment_otp_mode.description: Indicates whether OTP is preferred for later charge attempts. This is returned by the bank and may affect subsequent payment flows.

DirectDebitBindingData.description: Full binding view returned by `GET /binding/{binding_id}` and on terminal `/unbind` (fire-and-forget) and OTP-verify-unbind responses.

binding_id.description: UUID of the binding, generated by Singapay. This is the primary identifier for the binding and is used for all subsequent queries and references.

customer_ref.description: Merchant-side stable id for the customer (NOT the bank account number). Used to scope future bindings of the same customer.

bank_code.description: 3-digit BI/SNAP code of the target bank. Common values: `002` BRI, `008` Mandiri, `009` BNI, `011` Danamon, `014` BCA, `022` CIMB, `490` BNC.

masked_card.description: Masked bank account/card number returned by the bank after authorisation.

payment_otp_mode.description: Indicates whether OTP is preferred for later charge attempts. This value is returned by the bank and may affect subsequent payment flows.

redirect_url.description: Only populated while `status=PENDING_AUTH`. Treat as opaque — see `DirectDebitBindingInitiationData.redirect_url` for the full caveat.

expires_at.description: Only populated while `status=PENDING_AUTH`. Expiration time of the `redirect_url`.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the binding was created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the binding was last updated.

failure_reason.description: Failure reason when the binding or charge was rejected or expired.

DirectDebitUnbindOtpRequiredData.description: `data` payload returned by `POST /binding/{binding_id}/unbind` when the bank requires an OTP (typical for BNI, Danamon). The merchant must persist `otp_handoff` and submit it back through `/verify-otp` together with the OTP the customer received.

DirectDebitTransactionFees.description: Detailed fee breakdown materialised only for successful transactions. This object is absent for `PENDING`, `PENDING_OTP`, `FAILED`, and `EXPIRED` statuses.

DirectDebitTransactionData.description: `data` payload returned by `POST /charge`, `POST /verify-otp` (payment flow), and `GET /transaction/{transaction_id}`. `fees` is populated only when `status=SUCCESS`.

transaction_id.description: UUID of the transaction, generated by Singapay. This is the primary identifier for the transaction and is used for all subsequent queries and references.

binding_id.description: UUID of the `DirectDebitBinding` used for this transaction. This can be used to correlate charges to specific customer bank accounts.

account_id.description: Account ULID for the settlement destination, or numeric id when ULID lookup fails.

amount.description: Transaction amount.

requires_otp.description: Indicates whether the transaction requires OTP verification.

paid_at.description: Timestamp when the transaction was successfully paid. Null if not yet paid or if payment failed.

failure_reason.description: Human-readable failure explanation when the transaction is rejected or expires.

web_redirect_url.description: Hosted page for banks that require an in-browser flow.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the transaction was created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the transaction was last updated.

DirectDebitWebhookBindingEvent.description: Binding-lifecycle events. `succeeded` means the customer authorised the debit mandate (`data.status=ACTIVE`). `failed` covers cancel, reject, and expired hosted-webview sessions (`data.status` is `FAILED` or `EXPIRED`).

DirectDebitWebhookUnbindingEvent.description: Unbinding-lifecycle events. `succeeded` means the mandate is revoked (`data.status=UNBOUND`) and can no longer be charged. `failed` means the unbind did not complete; the binding typically remains `ACTIVE`.

DirectDebitWebhookTransactionEvent.description: Charge-lifecycle events. Terminal: `succeeded` / `failed` / `expired`. Intermediate OTP: `otp_required` (customer already has an OTP — call `POST /verify-otp`) and `otp_request_required` (Yokke-style — call `POST /request-otp` first, then `POST /verify-otp`). Plain `PENDING` does **not** emit a webhook.

CreatePaymentLinkV2Request.description: v2 simplifies the v1 body: `title`, `is_multiple_payment`, `is_unlimited_usage`, and `redirect_url_enabled` are no longer accepted — they are derived automatically from the other fields.

reff_no.description: Merchant reference number for this payment link.

description.description: Optional free-text description for the payment link.

payment_link_type.description: Must be exactly `total` or `items` (422 on any other value). Determines which of `total_amount` / `items` is required — the other one must not be sent at all: `total` requires `total_amount` and rejects `items` if sent (422); `items` requires `items` and rejects `total_amount` if sent (422), since it's computed from items server-side.

max_usage.description: Maximum number of successful payments allowed. Omit for a single-use link (defaults to `1`). `0` means unlimited. Any value greater than `1` makes this a multi-use link — `is_multiple_payment`/`is_unlimited_usage`/`required_customer_detail` are derived from this value and cannot be set directly.

expired_at.description: Optional expiration timestamp, any date/time string parseable by PHP (ISO 8601 recommended, e.g. `2026-08-10T00:00:00+07:00`). Must be in the future. Omit or send `null` to default to 24 hours from creation (D+1) — unlike v1, this is never left unset.

total_amount.description: Total payment amount. Required when `payment_link_type` is `total`; must not be sent at all when `payment_link_type` is `items` (422) — it's computed from `items` server-side instead, so sending both would be ambiguous. Minimum/maximum depend on merchant configuration and the resolved payment methods.

items.description: Line items. Required when `payment_link_type` is `items`; must not be sent at all when `payment_link_type` is `total` (422).

whitelisted_payment_method.description: Restricts accepted payment methods for this link. Omit, send `null`, or send an empty array to auto-select whichever active payment-link methods are actually eligible for the resolved `total_amount` — v2 never leaves this unrestricted the way v1 does. Each entry must be a valid payment method code.

success_redirect_url.description: URL to redirect the payer after successful payment. Must start with http:// or https://. Sending either this or `expired_redirect_url` automatically enables `redirect_url`.

expired_redirect_url.description: URL to redirect the payer after payment expiry. Must start with http:// or https://.

optional_metadata.description: Optional merchant-defined metadata stored with the payment link.

customer_name.description: Pre-fills the known customer name for a single-use link. Only allowed when `max_usage` resolves to `1`; sending this alongside a multi-use `max_usage` returns a 422. Required together with `customer_email`/`customer_phone` if any of the three is provided, and required (along with the other two) whenever `customer_notification_preference.payment_link_created` or `customer_notification_preference.payment_link_reminder` is non-empty — regardless of which channel(s) are selected.

customer_email.description: Pre-fills the known customer email. See `customer_name`.

customer_phone.description: Pre-fills the known customer phone number. Unlike `customer_name`/`customer_email`, not required merely by providing one of the other two fields — only required when `customer_notification_preference.payment_link_created` or `customer_notification_preference.payment_link_reminder` is non-empty.

required_customer_number.description: Only meaningful when `max_usage` > 1. Whether the payer must fill in a phone number at checkout. Defaults to `true` for multi-use links unless explicitly set to `false`.

required_customer_email.description: Only meaningful when `max_usage` > 1. Whether the payer must fill in an email at checkout. Defaults to `true` for multi-use links unless explicitly set to `false`.

customer_notification_preference.description: Which channels notify the customer at each lifecycle event. Only accepted for a single-use link. Having any channel (whatsapp or email) in either `payment_link_created` or `payment_link_reminder` requires `customer_name`, `customer_email`, AND `customer_phone` all three — not just the field the selected channel would use (422 if any is missing). WhatsApp incurs a fixed notification fee charged to the merchant's balance at send time; email is always free.

payment_link_created.description: Channels that notify the customer immediately when the link is created.

payment_link_reminder.description: Channels that notify the customer once, `reminder_period` `reminder_unit`(s) before `expired_at`. Non-empty requires `reminder_unit`/`reminder_period` to also be sent (422 if either is missing).

reminder_unit.description: Unit for `reminder_period`. Tied directly to `customer_notification_preference.payment_link_reminder`, not just to `reminder_period`: required (422 if missing) whenever `payment_link_reminder` has at least one channel, and prohibited (422 if sent) whenever it's empty or `customer_notification_preference` is omitted entirely.

reminder_period.description: How long before `expired_at` the reminder fires, in `reminder_unit` units: 1–24 for `hour`, 1–30 for `day`. Must resolve to a time strictly after `created_at` (422 otherwise). Same `payment_link_reminder`-tied required/prohibited 422 rule as `reminder_unit`.

UpdatePaymentLinkV2Request.description: True partial update — unlike v1's update (which recomputes several fields to their "not sent" defaults, silently clearing them when omitted), every field here is optional and any field left out of the request body is left completely untouched. `reff_no`, `title`, `payment_link_type`, `total_amount`, `items`, and `customer_name`/`customer_email`/`customer_phone` are immutable after creation and not accepted here.

description.description: Updates the payment link description. Send an empty string/`null` to clear it.

max_usage.description: Updates the usage cap. `0` means unlimited. Cannot be set below the current usage count (422). Also re-derives `is_multiple_payment`/`is_unlimited_usage`/`required_customer_detail`. Rejected with 422 if this payment link has `customer_name`/`customer_email`/`customer_phone` and/or a notification/reminder configuration set — those only work for single-use links, so changing max_usage could silently move the link to multi-use and break them. Omit to leave unchanged.

expired_at.description: Updates the expiration timestamp (must be in the future). Rejected with 422 if this payment link already has a reminder notification configured (i.e. `reminder_at` is set from `reminder_unit`/`reminder_period` sent at creation) — reminder_at is only computed once and would otherwise desync from the new expiry. Omit to leave unchanged.

status.description: Updates the payment link lifecycle status. Omit to leave unchanged.

whitelisted_payment_method.description: Updates the allowed payment method codes. Send `null`/an empty array to re-auto-select eligible methods based on the link's existing `total_amount`. Omit the field entirely to leave the current whitelist untouched.

success_redirect_url.description: Updates the success redirect URL. Omit to leave unchanged.

expired_redirect_url.description: Updates the expired redirect URL. Omit to leave unchanged.

optional_metadata.description: Updates the merchant-defined metadata. Omit to leave unchanged.

required_customer_number.description: Only applied when the link is (or is being made) multi-use. Omit to leave unchanged.

required_customer_email.description: Only applied when the link is (or is being made) multi-use. Omit to leave unchanged.

name.description: Line item name stored on the payment link.

quantity.description: Stored quantity for the line item.

unit_price.description: Stored unit price for the line item.

subtotal.description: Calculated line item subtotal (`quantity x unit_price`).

DirectDebitWebhookXSignature.name: X-Signature
DirectDebitWebhookXSignature.description: Lowercase hex HMAC-SHA512 of `{METHOD}:{ENDPOINT}:{ACCESS_TOKEN}:{SHA256_HEX(NORMALIZED_BODY)}:{X-Timestamp}`, keyed with the merchant `client_secret`. `METHOD` is `POST`. `ENDPOINT` is the **path only** of `direct_debit_notif_url` (no scheme, host, or query string). `ACCESS_TOKEN` is the bearer token from this request's `Authorization` header **without** the `Bearer ` prefix — it is a one-shot random token, not the merchant JWT. `NORMALIZED_BODY` is the JSON body with object keys recursively sorted (`ksort` / `SORT_STRING`) and re-encoded with `JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE | JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES` (no whitespace).

DirectDebitWebhookXTimestamp.name: X-Timestamp
DirectDebitWebhookXTimestamp.description: Unix epoch **seconds** (not ISO-8601) used when the signature was computed. Same value that appears as the last segment of the string-to-sign.

DirectDebitWebhookAuthorization.name: Authorization
DirectDebitWebhookAuthorization.description: `Bearer {ACCESS_TOKEN}`. The token is a 32-character random string generated per delivery. Use it only to recompute `X-Signature`; it is not a session JWT.

post.description: HTTP **POST** to `direct_debit_notif_url` for Direct Debit charges. Intermediate OTP events (one-shot on first transition): `direct-debit.transaction.otp_required` → `POST /verify-otp`; `direct-debit.transaction.otp_request_required` → `POST /request-otp` then `POST /verify-otp`.
